story_title: As a ConnectSphere user, I want to securely log in to the system so that I can access functionality appropriate to my role

acceptance_criteria.text: Given I have valid credentials, when I log in, then I am authenticated successfully.
Given I enter invalid credentials, when I attempt to log in, then access is denied and an appropriate error message is displayed.
Given I am logged in, when I access the system, then my role is identified.
Given I am logged in, when I access a function that my role is not authorised for, then access is denied.

test_cases.title: Valid credentials sign the user in and open the dashboard
test_cases.preconditions: Demo data is seeded. No one is signed in. On the "Log in" page.
test_cases.expected_result:
The button shows "Logging in…" while the request is in flight.
The browser moves to the Dashboard, headed "Welcome, Daniel Tan" with "Event Coordinator" beneath it, and the top bar shows the same role under the name.
No error message is shown.

test_cases.title: The signed-in chrome appears immediately, without a manual refresh
test_cases.preconditions: No one is signed in. On the "Log in" page, where no sidebar is shown.
steps: Look at the sidebar and the top bar without reloading the page
test_cases.expected_result:
The sidebar appears straight away with Dashboard, My Events and Notifications, and the top bar shows Rachel Ng.
No browser reload is needed to make the sidebar appear.

test_cases.title: After signing in, the user is returned to the page they first asked for
steps: Open the My Events page directly in the browser
Observe the page the browser lands on
test_cases.expected_result:
The browser lands on the "Log in" page showing the notice "Your session expired. Log in to continue where you left off."
After logging in, the browser opens My Events, not the Dashboard.

test_cases.title: The session survives a browser refresh
test_cases.preconditions: Signed in as Daniel Tan (daniel.tan@connectsphere.com / password123), on the Dashboard.
steps: Press F5 to reload the page
Wait for the page to finish loading
test_cases.expected_result:
The Dashboard reloads still signed in as Daniel Tan, still labelled "Event Coordinator".
The browser is not sent back to the "Log in" page.

test_cases.title: A wrong password is refused with an error message
test_cases.preconditions: Demo data is seeded. No one is signed in. On the "Log in" page.
test_cases.expected_result:
A red error message "Invalid email or password" is shown above the form.
The browser stays on the "Log in" page and no sidebar appears.

test_cases.title: An unknown email is refused with the same message as a wrong password
test_cases.preconditions: No account exists for nobody@connectsphere.com. No one is signed in. On the "Log in" page.
steps: Compare the message with the one seen in TC05
test_cases.expected_result:
The error message is "Invalid email or password" — word for word the same as TC05.
Nothing on screen reveals whether the account exists.

test_cases.title: An email that is not a valid address is refused with a message naming the problem
test_cases.preconditions: No one is signed in. On the "Log in" page.
test_cases.expected_result:
The message "Enter a valid email address" is shown against the Email field, which is outlined in red, so the user can see exactly which field to correct.
The browser stays on the "Log in" page.

test_cases.title: An empty password is refused with a message naming the problem
test_cases.preconditions: No one is signed in. On the "Log in" page.
test_cases.expected_result:
The message "Enter your password" is shown against the Password field, which is outlined in red.
The browser stays on the "Log in" page.

test_cases.title: A one-character password is treated as a wrong password, not a malformed one
test_cases.preconditions: No one is signed in. On the "Log in" page.
test_cases.expected_result:
The error message is "Invalid email or password" — the shortest allowed password is one character, so the attempt is checked as a credential rather than rejected as an empty field.
The browser stays on the "Log in" page.

test_cases.title: A deactivated account cannot log in, even with the correct password
test_cases.preconditions: Marcus Wong (marcus.wong@connectsphere.com) has been deactivated: open Prisma Studio (npx prisma studio), find the row in Users and set Is Active to false. No one is signed in. On the "Log in" page.
steps: Afterwards, set Is Active back to true in Prisma Studio
test_cases.test_data: Email: marcus.wong@connectsphere.com; Password: password123; Is Active: false
test_cases.expected_result:
The error message "This account has been deactivated. Contact your ConnectSphere administrator." is shown.
The browser stays on the "Log in" page and no dashboard is reached.

test_cases.title: An email typed with different capitalisation
test_cases.preconditions: Demo data is seeded. No one is signed in. On the "Log in" page.
test_cases.test_data: Email: Daniel.Tan@connectsphere.com (same address as TC01, different capitalisation); Password: password123
test_cases.expected_result: The user is signed in and the Dashboard opens, headed "Welcome, Daniel Tan" — an email address is not case sensitive, so this is the same account as TC01.

test_cases.title: The signed-in user's role is named on the dashboard
test_cases.preconditions: Demo data is seeded. No one is signed in.
steps: Log in as daniel.tan@connectsphere.com with password123
Read the subtitle under the welcome heading
Log out, then log in as marcus.wong@connectsphere.com with password123
Read the subtitle under the welcome heading again
test_cases.test_data: Accounts: daniel.tan@connectsphere.com (Coordinator), marcus.wong@connectsphere.com (Venue Staff); Password: password123
test_cases.expected_result:
Daniel Tan's dashboard is headed "Welcome, Daniel Tan", subtitled "Event Coordinator" and the section heading reads "Awaiting your review".
Marcus Wong's dashboard is headed "Welcome, Marcus Wong", subtitled "Venue Staff" and the section heading reads "Upcoming events".

test_cases.title: The navigation offered matches the role that is signed in
test_cases.preconditions: Demo data is seeded. No one is signed in.
steps: Log in as rachel.ng@meridianfina.com with password123
Write down every item in the sidebar
Log out, then log in as grace.lim@connectsphere.com with password123
Write down every item in the sidebar
test_cases.test_data: Accounts: rachel.ng@meridianfina.com (Organiser), grace.lim@connectsphere.com (Operations Manager); Password: password123
test_cases.expected_result:
Rachel Ng's sidebar reads Dashboard, My Events, Notifications.
Grace Lim's sidebar reads Dashboard, Assignments, All Events, Notifications.
The page layout, colours and top bar are identical for both — only the list of items differs.

test_cases.title: Logging out ends the session
test_cases.preconditions: Signed in as Daniel Tan (daniel.tan@connectsphere.com / password123), on the Dashboard.
steps: Click the account control in the top bar
Open the Dashboard directly in the browser
test_cases.expected_result:
Logging out returns the browser to the "Log in" page and the sidebar disappears.
Opening the Dashboard again lands back on "Log in" instead of showing Daniel Tan's dashboard.

test_cases.title: A signed-out visitor cannot reach a signed-in page
steps: Open the Dashboard directly in the browser
test_cases.test_data: Page requested: Dashboard, with no session
test_cases.expected_result:
The browser is sent to the "Log in" page with the notice "Your session expired. Log in to continue where you left off."
No dashboard content, event list or role name is shown at any point.

test_cases.title: A Coordinator cannot raise an event request
test_cases.preconditions: Signed in as Daniel Tan (daniel.tan@connectsphere.com / password123), a Coordinator. The sidebar offers no "New request" action.
steps: Open the "New event request" page directly in the browser
Enter "Coordinator authorisation check" into Event name
Enter "Checking that only an Organiser may raise a request" into Purpose
Enter a start and end date and time in the future
test_cases.test_data: Account: daniel.tan@connectsphere.com (Coordinator); Event name: Coordinator authorisation check; Expected attendance: 50
test_cases.expected_result:
The error message "Only an Event Organiser can raise an event request" is shown above the form.
The browser stays on the form and no draft is created — opening All Events afterwards shows no event named "Coordinator authorisation check".

test_cases.title: A stranger cannot give themselves a staff role when registering
test_cases.preconditions: No one is signed in. On the "Register" page.
test_cases.expected_result:
The dropdown offers exactly two options: "Event Organiser" and "Attendee".
Event Coordinator, Operations Manager, Venue Staff and Technical Support are not offered, so a staff account cannot be created by self-registration.

test_cases.title: An Organiser sees only their own client's events
test_cases.preconditions: Signed in as Rachel Ng (rachel.ng@meridianfina.com / password123), an Organiser at Meridian Financial Group. Budi Santoso (budi.santoso@nusantaratec.com) is an Organiser at Nusantara Tech Labs and has events of his own.
steps: Read the title and client of every event listed
Log out and log in as budi.santoso@nusantaratec.com with password123
Open My Events and compare the two lists
test_cases.test_data: Accounts: rachel.ng@meridianfina.com (Meridian Financial Group), budi.santoso@nusantaratec.com (Nusantara Tech Labs); Password: password123
test_cases.expected_result:
Rachel Ng's list contains only Meridian Financial Group events.
Budi Santoso's list contains only Nusantara Tech Labs events.
Neither list contains any event belonging to the other client.

test_cases.title: A tampered session token is not accepted
test_cases.preconditions: Signed in as Daniel Tan (daniel.tan@connectsphere.com / password123), on the Dashboard.
steps: Open the browser's developer tools and go to Application, then Local Storage
Change the last five characters of the value stored under "connectsphere_token"
test_cases.test_data: Stored key: connectsphere_token, with its last five characters altered
test_cases.expected_result:
The browser is sent to the "Log in" page.
No dashboard content or role name is shown — an altered token is treated as no session at all, not as a valid one.

open_questions: RESOLVED 2026-09-20. AC2 asks for an appropriate error message, but a malformed email or an empty password produced only "Validation failed" (TC07, TC08). src/app/login/page.tsx now maps the server's fieldErrors onto the fields using readServerError(), the same helper the Register page already used, and loginSchema carries written messages ("Enter a valid email address", "Enter your password") instead of Zod's defaults. Both cases were re-run and pass.

RESOLVED 2026-09-20. Email matching was case sensitive at login (TC11): Daniel.Tan@connectsphere.com was refused although daniel.tan@connectsphere.com with the same password succeeded. Both loginSchema and registerSchema now trim and lower-case the address before it is checked or stored, so capitalisation and a stray trailing space no longer change who you are. Covered by three new unit tests in src/lib/__tests__/validation.test.ts.

OPEN. The session token lasts eight hours (signSession in src/lib/auth.ts), which no acceptance criterion states and which a manual tester cannot sit out. Is eight hours the intended lifetime, and does it need a test of its own - for instance by shortening the expiry in a test build?

OPEN. The sidebar links every role to screens that do not exist yet: /queue, /venues, /equipment, /bookings, /browse, /registrations, /assignments and /notifications all return the Next.js 404 page. A tester following TC13 will click them. This is not a login defect, but it means an unauthorised-access test cannot be written against those screens yet, and Venue Staff and Technical Support currently have a sidebar where only Dashboard works.

OPEN. AC4 is about role, but the strongest denial the UI can currently show is a relationship one (TC18, one client's events hidden from another). Once the review queue and venue screens are built, AC4 should gain a case where a role opens a screen it is not authorised for and is told so, rather than reaching a 404.
